subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots inherit OpenClaw's host override policy unchanged, filter dependency overrides that conflict with plugin-owned runtime graphs, or only emit an Express 4 compatibility diagnostic?
rationale: The source evidence proves the conflict, but the permanent fix changes the dependency-ownership boundary for third-party plugin installs and may affect OpenClaw's security override policy.

options.title: Scope or filter managed-root overrides
options.body: Preserve OpenClaw's own Express 5/router dependency path while preventing host-only override pins from breaking plugin-owned transitive dependencies.

options.title: Add validator-only diagnostics
options.body: Keep current install semantics but fail earlier or with a clearer message for Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts.

options.title: Leave it to plugin packages
options.body: Require affected plugins to ship their own overrides or migrate to Express 5, accepting that OpenClaw managed installs can still surface opaque runtime failures.

recommendation.title: Scope or filter managed-root overrides
recommendation.body: Preserve OpenClaw's own Express 5/router dependency path while preventing host-only override pins from breaking plugin-owned transitive dependencies.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history routing candidate for managed npm root override propagation and plugin dependency docs.
